title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: pages 293-650 of the 'Longue Marche' continuation ('variations sur l'équation des lacets'). On the previous page Grothendieck takes the groupoid C_{1,1}^{ext} of groups with loop structure ('groupes à lacets') of type (1,1), i.e. fundamental groups of a once-punctured torus with the peripheral loop class as extra structure. He quotients it by the universal central automorphism -id. He gets an equivalence (55), C_{1,1}^{ext'} ≃ C_{0,3}. This lies over the equivalence Tors(GL(2,Z)/±1) ≃ Tors(Gp(1,Z)) induced by an isomorphism (57) between the relevant (extended) Teichmüller groups.

On this page he states his aim. He is giving a topological/'isotopic' paraphrase, in terms of fundamental groups with loop structure, of Legendre's theory relating elliptic curves and rational curves. That theory is the Legendre form y^2 = x(x-1)(x-λ): E\{0} → P^1 is the quotient by the elliptic involution x ↦ -x, branched over the three nonzero 2-torsion points. Up to now (55) was obtained indirectly, by knowing the two Teichmüller groups and writing an ad hoc homomorphism between them. He now wants to construct it directly from the groups π_{1,1} and π_{0,3}.

First step: for π' of type (1,1), Out_ext(π') ≅ GL(2,Z) contains a canonical element of order 2. It is the unique nontrivial element of the centre, denoted (-1)_{π'}, the topological elliptic involution. The margin NB notes that it preserves orientation, i.e. it has determinant +1 and lies in SL(2,Z), the orientation-preserving Teichmüller group.

Where this leads (next page): an outer action of Z/2 on π', hence a canonical extension 1 → π' → E → Z/2 → 1 (58). Concretely, E ≅ Z/2*Z/2*Z/2 is the orbifold fundamental group of (E\{0})/±1. Its splittings fall into exactly three π'-conjugacy classes, matching the three fixed points of -1 on E\{0} (the 2-torsion points). He then plans to use a largely conjectural theory of simultaneous loop structures under finite groups of outer operators to recover the genus-0 side, i.e. the sphere with the three branch points and the image of the origin.
errors: No mathematical error on this page. The claim that -1 is the unique nontrivial central element of Out_ext(π_{1,1}) ≅ GL(2,Z) is correct (centre = {±1}), and it has determinant +1, consistent with the NB.

Notational ambiguity, not an error: with the usual (g,ν) convention, π_{0,3} has finite extended Out (S_3×Z/2). An equivalence with a groupoid whose automorphism group is PGL(2,Z) = GL(2,Z)/±1 therefore suggests that 'C_{0,3}' here carries extra structure, e.g. the (0,4) situation with one distinguished puncture, or the orbifold sphere with three cone points of order 2. The page alone cannot settle this.

ideas.what: Legendre's relation between elliptic curves and rational curves (quotient by the elliptic involution, branched over 2-torsion), rephrased as an equivalence of groupoids of 'groupes à lacets' (types (1,1) and (0,3)) and of their Teichmüller torsors
ideas.modern_name: Legendre family / M_{1,1} vs M_{0,4} via E/±1; mapping class group isomorphism PSL(2,Z) ≅ Mod(S_{0,4})_{puncture}, extended version PGL(2,Z)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Legendre (classical); the mapping-class-group version is folklore (Birman–Hilden theory of the hyperelliptic involution, 1970s)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses M_{1,1} and M_{0,4} in the Teichmüller tower; this specific groupoid formulation appears only in these notes as far as known

ideas.what: Canonical central element (-1)_{π'} in Out_ext(π_{1,1}) ≅ GL(2,Z), orientation-preserving
ideas.modern_name: elliptic (hyperelliptic) involution as centre of the mapping class group SL(2,Z)

ideas.what: Programme: reconstruct the Legendre equivalence directly from the fundamental groups, via the Z/2-extension defined by the outer involution and its splittings (developed on the next page)
ideas.modern_name: Birman–Hilden lifting; orbifold fundamental group Z/2*Z/2*Z/2; correspondence between conjugacy classes of sections and fixed points (Nielsen/Kerckhoff realization, discrete analogue of the section conjecture)

deep.surprise_reason: This is an expository transitional page. It states the aim of rephrasing Legendre's elliptic/rational correspondence through groups with loop structure and singles out the classical central involution of GL(2,Z). The more substantive material (the extension and the conjectural theory of finite outer actions on groups with loop structure) is on the following page.
transcription_corrections: Line 2: the 'topologique-isotopique' reading is uncertain. 'topologique' appears struck or overwritten, with an insertion (perhaps 'isologique'); leave it as uncertain.

The end of the page should read roughly: 'il convient d'abord de noter qu'il y a dans Autext(π') un élément canonique d'ordre 2 — en fait l'unique élément non trivial du centre — noté comme de juste (−1)_{π'}.' The isolated 'Y' is the start of 'y a dans', 'loc' is probably an insertion of 'd'ordre' or similar, and '[?] symétrie - à-dire[?] comme de points' should be 'du centre — noté comme de juste'.
The marginal NB likely says roughly that (−1)_{π'} preserves orientation, i.e. has determinant +1, with a cross-reference; the mention of 'multiplicités' and '41' is unreliable.
